title: Non-Markovianity Induced By Pauli Twirling
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 August 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates how Pauli twirling, a common noise-tailoring technique, can induce non-Markovian behavior in the dynamics of open quantum systems.
motivation: Pauli twirling is widely used to convert arbitrary noise into stochastic Pauli channels, but its impact on the Markovianity of the resulting dynamics is not well understood. This work aims to clarify how twirling can introduce memory effects.
method: The authors analyze the effect of Pauli twirling on quantum process, likely using theoretical frameworks of quantum channels and non-Markovianity measures, possibly including numerical simulations or analytical derivations.
result: The paper demonstrates that Pauli twirling can induce non-Markovianity, challenging the assumption that twirling simplifies dynamics to a Markovian form. It provides conditions under which non-Markovian effects emerge.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need to account for potential non-Markovian behavior when applying Pauli twirling in quantum information tasks, and suggest that standard twirling may not always lead to the presumed Markovian approximation.
